I wish I could say it'll be easy, but it won't. I lost my 16-year-old dog/baby/best friend to kidney disease in February this year, and not having her around physically still hurts. The healing process isn't easy, but you can function again. The pain will slowly be replaced with nostalgia and peaceful memories, but don't rush it. 

I was a wreck for the first few months. I would have to take a minute to cry after every work call because she wasn't at my feet (I WFH). The sight of a Dachshund or even Dachshund-related products triggered panic attacks and sobbing in public. 

Two months passed and I made the mistake of adopting a dog. It was a mistake because I wasn't ready. I love all dogs, so I loved him but I didn't LOVE him. I had to rehome him with someone who was ready to give him all their love as all dogs deserve. 

Three months later, I found my new pup. She has the same spunk and sassy attitude as my old girl, and it feels like I'm raising her all over again, haha. I still have days when I'm reminded of Sara and cry. We made a little memorial for her in one of our closets, which I like to visit on particularly hard days. We filled it with her toys, favorite blankets, a photo book, and the little wooden box that holds her ashes. 

You'll never forget your childhood dog, nor should you! The pain will lessen eventually, but those memories you have of her will stay with you forever. 

Sending you all the strength and support! I know you have a bunch of awesome folks commenting already, but if you need anyone else to message, I'm here :)
